note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), read offline from the bundled owb-am text, per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 that every Amharic work quotes OWB. Every quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim, replacing the 1962 UBS wording and the OT renderings made in its register: Bounds's long block quotations of the prayer narratives (Jacob, Samson, Solomon, Moses, Elijah, Hezekiah, Ezra, Nehemiah, Daniel, Paul), his cited verses, and the phrases he quotes again inside his own sentences.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse or range, the shortest span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'. Where OWB opens an inner quotation inside a verse, the inner marks are ‹ › (and ‘ ’ one level further in). `self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are allusions, the author's own paraphrases in the third person, and the Revised Version renderings he compares with the AV.

Judgement calls. 1 Kings 17:1 'before whom I stand' is OWB «የማገለግለው» ('whom I serve'); because Bounds builds Elijah's chapter on the phrase and sets Gabriel's 'I stand in the presence of God' (Luke 1:19, OWB «በእግዚአብሔር ፊት እቆማለሁ») beside it, the discussion carries a one-time gloss (— ማለትም በፊቱ የቆምሁት —). Jonah 2:2 'the belly of hell' is OWB «ከሙታን ዓለም ጥልቅ», and Bounds's echoes of it follow. Solomon's 'I am but a little child' (1 Kings 3:7) is OWB «ገና ትንሽ ልጅ ነኝ», echoed identically (decision jeremiah-only-a-child). 1 Samuel 15:11 OWB reads «ሳሙኤልም ተቆጣ» ('Samuel was angry') for the AV 'it grieved Samuel'; it is quoted as OWB has it and Bounds's comment on Samuel's grief stands. 1 Timothy 2:8 'without wrath' is OWB «ከቁጣ … ርቀው», and the author's word-study of «ቁጣ» follows OWB's spelling. 'Behold, he prayeth' (Acts 9:11) is OWB «እርሱ አሁን እየጸለየ ነው». Two KJV-joined quotations (Psalm 90:12 with 90:17; 2 Corinthians 1:10-11 with Philippians 1:18, as the English prints them) are each quoted from OWB piece by piece.
